quote: Ring out the old, ring in the new, ring, happy bells, across the snow: the year is going, let him go; ring out the false, ring in the true.
source: Alfred Tennyson, In Memoriam A.H.H., section CIV, lines 5 to 8 (Edward Moxon, 1850; CVI in the final text)
note: Section number corrected. In the 1850 Moxon first edition the Ring out, wild bells poem is section CIV; it became CVI only after Tennyson inserted section LIX in 1851 and section XXXIX in 1869. The wording is the first edition’s.

evidence.where: Project Gutenberg 70950, the transcription of the Edward Moxon 1850 first edition, downloaded and grepped; the volume has 129 sections, the stanza stands under CIV, and CVI in that volume is I will not shut me from my kind
evidence.edition: In Memoriam (Edward Moxon, Dover Street, 1850), first edition
evidence.locator: section CIV, second stanza, lines 5 to 8

reason: The refutation stands: the 1850 edition numbers the poem CIV, so the earlier verdict’s CVI pointed at a different poem in the edition it named. The wording holds exactly. Not shipped, no near match, Tennyson at 0 of 3, not banned.
